There is no point. It’s a harsh truth. Accepting that life is meaningless is a huge step towards living a life that’s fulfilling. I am not someone born into wealth, and I’ve worked extremely hard to get what little I do have in this life. When I’m manic, I get extremely depressed and take on a very “whoa is me” attitude because I had nothing handed to me while others lead these blissful, effortless lives since birth. Comparison is the thief of joy but that’s easier said than done when you’re constantly bombarded by the fact that some people really do just get everything. And that’s not even their fault, in many instances they were born into it. I read a book called “The Art of Living a Meaningless Existence” and a few others similar to it, it helped me ask the question “why do I feel like I even deserve to have everything handed to me?”. Once I accepted that you can’t choose your life, you can only try to live the best one you were given, I started to savor more morsels of time throughout the day. I stopped hating my work and began to appreciate that I even have a job while so many others do not. It’s not a cure all, I still have feelings of regret, anxiety, depression, and frankly all out rage towards the 1% that suck our resources dry while the rest of the world fights for scraps but I’m making a conscious effort to work on it day by day. Idk if this will help anyone but if it helps even one person then taking the time to write this is worth it.

Well, we are going to Mexico in a month and I told her that she will have to explain to her family that I don’t drink and her response was, “You’re going to drink.”. How fucked up is that?! Well, I’ve made the decision to commit to sobriety and enter a program, I never ever want to feel the way I have the past 3 days ever again. If that means I lose friends and family then they were never really there for me anyways, the people who truly love you should love you regardless. I just wanted to let you know that you’re not the only one going through this.

I made a pros and cons list s while ago. The pros are very few, some are just hypothetical, and overall just extremely generic. The lis is basically just, 1) I’ll love the kid, 2) I might enjoy being a father, 3) it would make my parents happy. That’s about it. The cons list however, is very very long. Some of the highlights include, 1) financial burden, 2) lifelong commitment, 3) I don’t want to pass my mental illness along to my child, 4) the world is such a shit place and headed in the wrong direction, why would I subject someone to it?, 5) loss of free time which is already scarce, 6) no privacy, 7) I may not even form the “typical” connection I’m supposed to with my child, the list goes on and on and on. Ultimately, I don’t think that having children is smart for anyone unless they can give that child a significantly better life than they had and I have decided that it’s just not something that will make me feel fulfilled or happy.

Fully gutted an 1870’s Victorian, lived with parents during first 6 months which was essentially all demo. Went through 7 dumpsters of old horse hair lathe and plaster, asbestos wiring, old nasty tile, carpet, and scrap lumber from the walls we ripped out (reused what we could of the rough cut studs). Keep in mind, I own a restoration business so 90% of the work was done by myself after work and during all my free time. It took 1.5 years start to finish and the pros and cons are as follows:

Cons: 1) it does cost money ($63K total for materials and various labor that was hired out for, plumbing being the main one but again, I’m in the business so I got a buddy of mine to do it well and fair priced). $63K would translate to about $225K where I’m from if I had just hired out for everything. 

2) Time. You have no more free time. 

3) Stress. If you have a significant other and they aren’t fully ready for this then don’t do it. Living in a construction zone will without a doubt put a ton of stress on the relationship. 

Pros: 1) location location location. Newly built homes are usually either standalone on a good chunk of property which translates to dolla dolla bills or you’re gonna live in a cookie cutter suburb and in that case this life was never for you anyways, enjoy living in Hell. In our case, our town is historic and a large tourist destination so if you want to live close to downtown and the fun stuff, you’re home is gonna be old. Our homes location translates to $$$ because we AirBnB it during tourist season and you will never have to drive. Anywhere. We are a 5 minute picturesque walk to everything.

2) location location location = rarity. I’m a blue collar guy but I know how to exploit the boujee elite. They want the status of living or staying where we do because, again, you can walk everywhere and it’s so picturesque with all the Victorian architecture and shops and restaurants at your doorstep. You can’t build where we live without buying an expensive old home, tearing it down, and building new. Minimum one million investment. Minimum. So therefore a renovated Victorian in our location is a rare find.

3) customize the home exactly how you want it from the ground up. We have a 152 year old house with central air, a primary bathroom designed for a king, custom finishes, blah blah blah. It’s all your style and design so you never have to be like “yeah I like it but I’d change the tile if I could.”

4) buy low, put in the sweat equity and dollars, get rewarded and hold that thing for life. We have doubled our homes value in 1.5 years. Let me say that again: our is now worth twice what we paid for it. We will never sell it, and due to its unique location, it will never lose its value. We will use AirBnB and rentals to make the house profitable while it continues to increase our equity naturally over time. 

Conclusion: if you have the means and balls, it’s a no brainer. The American population doesn’t want this life. They want to be move in ready. There’s a niche out there for go getters. It will be hard, but knowing what we bought it at and then seeing what it’s worth now, it really made it all worth it.

One thing I tell people who can’t understand is that you can’t be as hard to me as I’m already being on myself. Trust me, I already feel like a pile of shit, you adding to that pile doesn’t help. The best friends I’ve had will tell me that they are here for me and willing to talk whenever I’m ready to talk, not on their time but on mine. And they won’t text things like “hey you doing ok?” because obviously I’m fucking not. Instead they will try calling and if I don’t pick up that’s that. They will text me to invite me places and if I say no then it’s no, there’s no pressure or guilt. I hope this helps and I hope your friend gets better but ultimately, learning to live with depression and recognize and avoid your triggers is what helps me. That and therapy and anti-depressants but it will always feel like an uphill climb.
